claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain under high-temperature mechanical loading than commercially pure tungsten.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater toughness under high-temperature mechanical loading than commercially pure tungsten.
The multielement composition of equimolar WTaTiVZr produces severe lattice distortions.
Severe lattice distortions in WTaTiVZr modify and hinder conventional dislocation motion.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr promotes enhanced dynamic recovery during high-temperature deformation.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr activates deformation twinning.
Deformation twinning can contribute to high strength, ductility, and fracture toughness.
Dynamic recovery and deformation twinning jointly increase the work-hardening capability of WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
Dynamic recovery and deformation twinning delay crack nucleation in WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
Elevated-temperature mechanical behavior of TaTiVWZr has previously been studied and compared with pure tungsten.
Under matched high-temperature testing, WTaTiVZr will have a significantly higher strain to failure than pure tungsten.
Under matched high-temperature testing, WTaTiVZr will have higher fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
Deformed WTaTiVZr will exhibit altered dislocation arrangements relative to pure tungsten.
Deformed WTaTiVZr will contain more deformation twins than pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism applies under high-temperature conditions relevant to plasma-facing components.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at lower temperatures or when grain-size variation or phase segregation predominates.
The relative contributions of dynamic recovery and deformation twinning remain quantitatively uncertain and may depend on testing conditions.
Matching grain size and processing history and applying identical loading in an inert atmosphere provides a controlled comparison between WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten.
